title: Cross-tenancy safeguard: rapid diagnosis & staged feature‑gate rollback for asymmetric inference degradations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Create an actionable playbook and lightweight automation to rapidly contain asymmetric canary regressions that affect only a subset of tenants or deployment tiers (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).

Background: Over the last 12 months we've observed several regressions introduced during model rollouts where only certain tenant slices (by size, routing region, or dedicated pool) experienced quality degradation or latency spikes. These asymmetric failures are harder to detect and remediate because global health metrics can remain green while affected customers escalate. Current rollback flows are manual and often require cross-team coordination that delays mitigation.

Scope: This ticket covers: (1) a diagnostic checklist for asymmetric regressions; (2) a staged feature-gate rollback pattern that works across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments; (3) a set of automation scripts to accelerate tenant quarantine, traffic split adjustments, and KV-cache reconciliation; and (4) customer communication templates and SLA-sensitive mitigation steps.

Out-of-scope: full rewrite of rollout system (will be tracked separately), long-term telemetry redesign not required for immediate mitigation.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A documented, tested checklist that a pager engineer can follow to: detect asymmetric degradations, identify affected tenant slice, and perform an emergency staged rollback within 30 minutes.
2) Automation (scripts/ops commands) that can: flip a feature-gate per-tenant or per-pool, re-route up to 20% of traffic to fallback model variants, and flush/prime KV cache for affected nodes.
3) Runbook verified in drill with SRE/Support and a playbook entry added to the oncall rotations.
4) Customer-facing comms templates and escalation matrix added to the customer-support runbook.
runbook_steps:
Step 0 - Triage: Confirm the signal is asymmetric vs global. Look at per-tenant latency/quality heatmap (Dashboards > inference-per-tenant). Check model-eval regressions linked to the rollout.
Step 1 - Contain: If slice confirmed, enable 'quarantine routing' for the slice: shift 100% of the slice to a local fallback variant (feature-gate flip: runtime.fallback.<slice-id> = true). For Dedicated pools, bump to reserved fallback capacity. For Private, instruct customer operator via secure channel and offer a hotpatch artifact if requested.
Step 2 - Traffic split: Initiate staged rollback: 100% -> 75% fallback -> 50% -> 0% for new model over 20 minutes while monitoring quality metrics. Use automated canary controller to orchestrate.
Step 3 - KV cache reconciliation: For stateful caches, run kv-reconcile --slice <id> to ensure prefix caches are invalidated consistently across mixed model versions. If mismatch detected, trigger cache-warm priming against fallback prior to redirecting traffic.
Step 4 - Communication: Notify affected customers via Support with templated message. Internally update Slack #incidents and create a cross-team bridge including PM, SRE, and Solutions Eng.
Step 5 - Root cause & fix: After stable rollback, capture traces and a sampling of failed requests, create a short repro and link to PRs. Triage into the next sprint or hotfix as needed.
Step 6 - Postmortem: Run blameless postmortem within 72 hours and update rollout automation to close any gaps discovered.
Contingency - Fast-forward hotpatch: If rollback causes unacceptable customer disruption, escalate to hotpatch channel: create a signed artifact with pinned weights of previous model and coordinate across Private customer operators for side-loading.
Contingency - Customer-specific pinning: For high-value customers on Dedicated/Private, prepare tenant-pin plan with Solutions Eng and Sales for a bilateral rollback cadence and SLA credits as needed.

notes: Tradeoffs: Full automated rollback across Private deployments requires customer-side automation or signed hotpatch process; for now we rely on operator handshake for safety and compliance.
Telemetry gaps: Need higher-fidelity per-tenant quality signals (synthetic evals per model variant). Proposed follow-up: a lightweight per-tenant eval runner to run against canary cohorts.

Rollout options considered: immediate global rollback (fast but noisy) vs staged tenant-aware rollback (slower but minimizes blast radius). Chose staged tenant-aware as default for asymmetric signals.
